brief: Bad vs Good vs Great hooks — the 6 patterns top creators use to stop the scroll.

slots.body: Bad hooks give away the answer in the first line. Great hooks open a loop your reader must close. The gap between what they know and want to know is your leverage.
slots.note: Use before a payoff or reveal.

slots.body: Saying many tips is vague and easy to skip. Attaching an odd number creates a concrete promise. Seven ways feels more trustworthy than several ways ever will.
People scroll past generic advice they have already heard. They pause when you name a specific mistake they are making. Relief comes from knowing there is a fix.
slots.note: Call out the error, then offer salvation.

slots.body: Starting with stats feels like a report nobody asked for. Starting in the middle of a moment creates instant immersion. Show the scene, then teach the lesson.
slots.note: Drop readers into action, not exposition.

slots.body: Agreeing with common wisdom is invisible in a crowded feed. Challenging a sacred belief triggers an emotional need to read on. Make them prove you wrong.
Learn this skill feels like homework without a deadline. Learn this in five minutes feels achievable before lunch. Compress the timeline to remove friction.
slots.note: Shorter time horizons increase saves and shares.

slots.body: Save this carousel as your swipe file. Great hooks are built, not born.
